ideas.pitch: An automated cryptographic protocol flaw finder targeted at modern CTF challenge binaries.
ideas.problem_statement: The competition will challenge participants across areas such as penetration testing, reverse engineering, cryptography, and vulnerability exploitation
ideas.title: CryptoFlag Auditor
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages advanced cryptographic analysis patterns similar to previous hackathon-winning architectures, giving teams an edge in speed during time-crunch CTFs.

ideas.pitch: An autonomous agentic vulnerability scanner that identifies web-app and binary misconfigurations to capture hidden flags.
ideas.problem_statement: Identify vulnerabilities, apply technical problem-solving skills, and capture hidden flags to score points.
ideas.title: AgenticRedTeam
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly automates the manual grunt work of standard CTF challenges using agentic pipelines, mirroring the grand-prize winning automated hacking concepts.

ideas.pitch: A localized reverse-engineering assistant that maps out control flow graphs and spots obfuscated flag strings in binary blobs.
ideas.problem_statement: The competition will challenge participants across areas such as penetration testing, reverse engineering, cryptography, and vulnerability exploitation
ideas.title: RevGuard Decompiler
ideas.why_it_could_win: Solves a notoriously tedious part of reverse engineering competitions by combining graph intelligence with pattern matching.

ideas.pitch: A privacy-preserving local storage application for capturing and organizing classified CTF flags securely.
ideas.problem_statement: Identify vulnerabilities, apply technical problem-solving skills, and capture hidden flags to score points.
ideas.title: ZeroKnow Vault
ideas.why_it_could_win: Brings military-grade zero-knowledge encryption principles to a domain where credential and flag leakage can cost teams the match.

ideas.pitch: A real-time network topology visualizer and simulation toolkit for testing lateral movement and privilege escalation routes.

ideas.title: NetSim Attack Path
ideas.why_it_could_win: Visually stunning 3D threat mapping ensures strong presentation scores, echoing previous A10 Networks hackathon-winning mechanics.
